answer: Launching N sybils costs N bonded stakes plus the sink cost of building trust through real work; below a threshold the attacker loses more than any reward, making mass identity creation economically irrational. Each agent stakes a bond at the wharf registry before any voyage, and a lightweight score kernel weights votes by stake age times verified task history, so fresh identities start near zero. From once0008's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
